core.text: Concrete ablation-and-migration comparison: retain P1 source-to-rack transfer and P2 counting, correction and sealing; migrate their carrier supply from powered trolley R2 to hand carrier R3. Preserve identifiers, arrival-order inspection and B9 correction. Vehicle selection is permitted within P1; this does not establish an independent interface intervention.

Closest rival is the original link: trolley B4-B7 at 0-3, trolley B8-B11 at 3-6, hand B12 at 6-7. Migrated link: nine consecutive hand trips at 0-9. Inspect continuously from 0; B9 runs 8-10 in both. Model-derived predictions: both release all twelve by 13 without unloading waits; original transfer labor is seven minutes, migrated labor nine. The original therefore wins the stated preference.

Feasible separating probe: execute each specified schedule in the stipulated model and compare identity unloads, completed correct releases, occupied intervals and boundary rack states. Attribute nine source arrivals separately from twelve releases. P2 requires thirteen occupied minutes in either successful sequence. Counting marks cannot substitute for seals.

residue.text: Compare parent-alone and broken-link controls using legal idling. P2 alone releases only initial B1-B3. P1 alone cannot complete nine unloads because no inspections free rack space. Broken-link idling collapses to a parent-alone control. Independent co-presence with active successful P1 but disconnected P2 is unavailable: P1 necessarily unloads onto the same rack. Do not invent floor storage or a bypass to manufacture it.

Defeat an interaction-specific explanation if the seven-versus-nine transfer burden is accounted for entirely by P1 trip duration and capacity, while P2 processing stays fixed. Parent-only cost accounting already predicts this comparison. Necessary material dependence does not establish a novel interaction or beneficial migration; changed vehicle timing and capacity must remain explicit.

These are finite-model deductions, not observed trials or a global-optimality proof. Burden falls on the same transfer clerk; migration avoids trolley charge while adding two occupied minutes in these sequences. Packing discrepancy cause and later request adaptation remain unknown; neither supplies evidence for an additional mechanism.

tension.account_a: A coordinated supply connection contributes an interaction beyond each unchanged parent function.
tension.account_b: P1 vehicle arithmetic explains comparative labor; fixed P2 processing explains completion timing.
tension.prediction_a: A distinguishable legal link control should change combined output beyond predictions from parent schedules alone; otherwise this interaction claim fails.
tension.prediction_b: Parent schedules alone predict twelve releases at 13 under both links, with seven versus nine transfer minutes; separate active disconnected co-presence is infeasible.
